The '''Xanaq Civil War''' was the short conflict that followed the collapse of the [[Bu Dynasty]] and preceded the founding consolidation of the [[People's Federation of Xanaqu]] in 1936.

The extracted Xanaqu source describes it as a small, roughly year-long war between the [[Red Army of Xanaqu|Red Army]] under [[Xun Tao]] and republican forces associated with [[General Cheng Jin]] and the [[Xanaq Republicans]].

== Background ==

In late 1934, Xun Tao and the [[Taoist Party]] led demonstrations against the declining Bu Dynasty. After the dynasty collapsed, republican forces attempted to establish a rival state in the north.

The conflict was therefore both a succession crisis and an ideological struggle over what would replace the dynasty: a republican state led by former dynastic military figures or a people's federation built around worker councils and Taoist political principles.

== Outcome ==

The Red Army defeated the republican forces. The source notes that many republican members were pardoned by Xun Tao, suggesting that the new state chose incorporation over mass purge during its founding settlement.

The victory cleared the way for the People's Federation of Xanaqu, founded in 1936 under the principles later associated with the [[Taoist Manifesto]].
